---
description-meta: "Step conversion by device with 95% intervals, and the mobile minus desktop gap at every checkout step."
title: "Checkout funnel"
pagetitle: "Checkout funnel"
---

```{ojs}
//| output: false
import {
  loadResults,
  dataAlert,
  gapChart,
  dataTable,
  formatPercent,
  formatPoints,
  formatCount,
  intervalText,
  STEP_LABELS,
} from "./charts.js"

results = loadResults({
  conversion: FileAttachment("sources/results/funnel_step_conversion.csv"),
  gaps: FileAttachment("sources/results/funnel_mobile_gap.csv"),
  orderCheck: FileAttachment("sources/results/funnel_checkout_order_check.csv"),
})
```

```{ojs}
//| classes: data-alert-slot
dataAlert(results.missing)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
conversion = results.data.conversion
gaps = results.data.gaps
widestGap = gaps.reduce((worst, row) => (row.gap_low < worst.gap_low ? row : worst), {
  gap_low: Infinity,
})
widestStep = STEP_LABELS.get(widestGap.step_name)?.toLowerCase() ?? "—"
widestShortfall = Number.isFinite(widestGap.gap_low)
  ? (Math.abs(widestGap.gap_low) * 100).toFixed(1)
  : "—"
check = results.data.orderCheck[0] ?? {}
```

::: {.lede}
No step converts mobile shoppers worse than desktop shoppers by more than the noise allows. The
largest shortfall the data still allows is ${widestShortfall} points, at ${widestStep}.
:::

Each step is measured on its own: of the sessions that had the previous step's event, the share
that also had this step's event, in any order. The sample's timestamps cannot order the checkout
steps (see [method](method.qmd)), so the rates are not multiplied into one session-to-purchase
rate.

```{ojs}
//| classes: slot-gap
gapChart(Plot, gaps, {
  width,
  title: "Every mobile minus desktop gap has an interval that crosses zero",
  subtitle: "Difference in step conversion, percentage points, with 95% Newcombe intervals. Sessions, 1 Nov 2020 to 31 Jan 2021.",
})
```

```{ojs}
//| classes: slot-table
devices = [
  { key: "mobile", label: "Mobile" },
  { key: "desktop", label: "Desktop" },
  { key: "tablet", label: "Tablet" },
]
byStep = conversion.length === 0 ? [] : [...STEP_LABELS.keys()].map((stepName) => {
  const row = { step: STEP_LABELS.get(stepName), stepName }
  for (const { key } of devices) {
    row[key] = conversion.find((r) => r.step_name === stepName && r.device_category === key) ?? {}
  }
  return row
})

dataTable({
  caption: "Step conversion by device, with 95% Wilson intervals",
  rows: byStep,
  highlight: (row) => row.stepName === "add_payment_info",
  columns: [
    { label: "Step", value: (row) => row.step },
    ...devices.flatMap(({ key, label }) => [
      { label, value: (row) => formatPercent(row[key].conversion), numeric: true },
      {
        label: `${label} interval`,
        value: (row) => intervalText(row[key].conversion_low, row[key].conversion_high),
        numeric: true,
      },
      {
        label: `${label} sessions`,
        value: (row) => formatCount(row[key].sessions_entered),
        numeric: true,
      },
    ]),
  ],
})
```

```{ojs}
//| classes: slot-table
dataTable({
  caption: "Mobile minus desktop, percentage points",
  rows: gaps,
  highlight: (row) => row.step_name === "add_payment_info",
  columns: [
    { label: "Step", value: (row) => STEP_LABELS.get(row.step_name) },
    { label: "Mobile", value: (row) => formatPercent(row.mobile_conversion), numeric: true },
    { label: "Desktop", value: (row) => formatPercent(row.desktop_conversion), numeric: true },
    { label: "Gap", value: (row) => formatPoints(row.gap), numeric: true },
    {
      label: "95% interval",
      value: (row) => `${formatPoints(row.gap_low)} to ${formatPoints(row.gap_high)}`,
      numeric: true,
    },
  ],
})
```

## Why the funnel ignores event order

In ${formatPercent(check.shipping_before_checkout / check.checkout_sessions)} of
${formatCount(check.checkout_sessions)} checkout sessions, the first shipping event is
timestamped before checkout begins. In
${formatPercent(check.purchases_without_add_to_cart / check.purchase_sessions)} of purchasing
sessions there is no add-to-cart event, because the cart was filled in an earlier visit. A funnel
that requires every earlier step in order would drop both groups and report drop-off that never
happened; the step-pair rule counts them from checkout onward.
